_readme: HAND-LABELLED GROUND TRUTH FOR COUNTRY CLASSIFICATION.
The question asked of each (record, country) pair was NOT 'does this
document mention the country'. It was: is this document's SCOPE defined by
that country? A rule that terminates Temporary Protected Status for Yemen
is about Yemen. A rule about appellate procedure that cites the name of a
US-Guatemala transfer agreement is not about Guatemala, and a subscriber
monitoring Guatemala should not receive it.
That distinction is the whole point of the dimension, so it is what is
labelled, one pair at a time, with the reason.
THE POOL IS PRECISION-ONLY, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.
Every pair the classifier produced is labelled here, so precision is a real
measurement. Recall is NOT measured: finding the false negatives would mean
reading all 544 records for unstated country scope, and there is no honest
shortcut. Recall for this dimension is unknown and is reported as unknown.
Two of the labels below are genuinely arguable and are marked 'debatable'.
They are scored as errors, because a monitoring product should lose an
argument about whether a match was justified, not win it.

The rule explicitly exempts aliens returning from Canada. That is scope, not a mention.
The rule terminates TPS for SOUTH Sudan. 'Sudan' matched inside 'South Sudan'. Sudan has its own separate TPS designation, so this would send a Sudan subscriber a rule about a different country.
A rule about Board of Immigration Appeals appellate procedure. Guatemala appears only inside the quoted title of a US-Guatemala transfer agreement the rule cites.
Same rule, same agreement title. Canada is genuine scope here; Guatemala is part of the cited agreement's name.
A rule on alien registration generally. Canada appears in a list describing Form I-185, the Canadian border crossing card, not in the rule's scope.

The text says AMERICAN Samoa, a United States territory, in a passage about who is a US national. The independent state of Samoa is a different place, and this is the classifier confusing them.

The visa bond pilot names no countries at all: it says the list 'will be announced on travel.state.gov'. The record correctly carries scopeDefinedElsewhere, and classifying any country on top of that contradicts it.
The same visa bond pilot rule, whose country list is delegated to the State Department and named nowhere in the document.

The rule removes automatic EAD extension for every category. The Compact of Free Association countries appear in a footnote listing one affected category. Arguable, because the effect on those nationals is real; scored as an error because the rule is not about them.
